overview: This 116-page file documents American patent and unfair competition concerns involving Japan from 1930 to 1939. Company complaints, consular reports, legal memoranda, advertising materials, and a translated patent-law amendment trace disputes over sewing machines, industrial processes, printing equipment, toy boats, and watch straps. State Department replies distinguish diplomatic assistance from remedies available under Japanese and U.S. law.
interest: Company catalogues and case correspondence show how commercial pressures shaped requests for diplomatic help with patent disputes.
